_meta.description: Single source of truth for every numeric assumption in the DRI digital twin.

provenance_status_values.verified: Value read directly from the cited source text in ../data/text/.
provenance_status_values.needs_citation: Plausible engineering default, NOT yet traced to a source in this repository. Must be cited before submission.
provenance_status_values.physical_constant: Thermodynamic or stoichiometric constant (molar mass, standard enthalpy, Cp).
provenance_status_values.derived: Computed by the model from other parameters; listed here only as a validation target.

_meta.calibration_plant: Dey et al. (2015), Case Studies in Thermal Engineering 6, 1-15. 30 t/h ore feed, 18.9 t/h sponge iron (453.6 TPD). Full measured material + heat balance in Tables 4-11.
_meta.units_convention: Masses in kg per tonne of DRI unless stated. Energy in kJ internally; Gcal only for display. 1 Gcal = 4.1868e6 kJ.

plant.capacity_tpd.source: User input. Indian sponge iron kilns are typically 100/350/500 TPD.
plant.capacity_tpd.notes: 100 TPD is the standard Indian MSME kiln module.

plant.utilization.notes: Capacity utilisation; CEEW survey notes idling but gives no single figure.

plant.operating_days.source: Engineering default (35 d/yr planned shutdown for kiln relining).

coal.rate_mode.source: Dey et al. (2015) Section 3.6 'Model development for coal consumption' derives the coal requirement from the kiln heat demand rather than assuming it: Qs + Qa + Qp + Qloss + mm*lambda = mc*NHV*(0.433).
coal.rate_mode.source_file: Energy survey of the coal based sponge iron industry_Nishant R Dey et al
coal.rate_mode.notes: In 'solve' mode the coal rate is whatever closes the energy balance for the given coal quality and loss set, and is then validated against CEEW's surveyed 0.9-1.6 t-coal/t-DRI band. This is the intended default: it makes coal consumption a model RESULT instead of a free input.

coal.rate_t_per_t_dri.source: TERI: 'calorific value of coal as 5200 kcal/kg, and coal to iron ratio of 0.95'. CEEW range: imported 0.9-1.1, domestic 1.4-1.6 t-coal/t-DRI.
coal.rate_t_per_t_dri.source_file: ENERGY-EFFICIENT TECHNOLOGY OPTIONS FOR DIRECT REDUCTION OF IRON PROCESS_TERI
coal.rate_t_per_t_dri.notes: Used directly only when coal.rate_mode is 'specified'. In 'solve' mode the coal rate is derived by closing the energy balance and this value becomes the starting guess plus a cross-check. 0.95 is TERI's IMPORTED-coal ratio; pairing it with Dey's domestic-grade coal analysis (23.7% ash, 5,384 kcal/kg) is internally inconsistent and leaves the energy balance ~11% short.

kiln.reaction_temp_c.source_file: Decarbonizing rotary kiln induction furnace based sponge iron production_Nishant Bhardwaj et al

kiln.ambient_temp_c.source: Reference state for all sensible-heat terms.

kiln.excess_air_frac.source: Engineering default; Dey computes air from stoichiometric O2 demand with no explicit excess-air figure.

kiln.unburnt_vm_carbon_frac.source: Dey et al. (2015) Table 10: 'Unburnt V.M.C. 3,258.76' of 13,286.77 kg/h coal carbon
kiln.unburnt_vm_carbon_frac.source_file: Energy survey of the coal based sponge iron industry_Nishant R Dey et al
kiln.unburnt_vm_carbon_frac.notes: Largest single carbon inefficiency in the kiln. Leaves the kiln as hydrocarbons and is post-combusted in the after-burner chamber, so it still becomes CO2 at the stack.

kiln.h2_burnt_in_kiln_frac.source: Dey et al. (2015) Section 3.3 assumptions: '1/3 of H2 from feed end coal reports to ABC as CH4'. Feed-end coal is 13,990 of 21,720 kg/h total coal (64.4%), so the unburnt share of coal hydrogen is 0.644/3 = 0.215 and the share burnt inside the kiln is 0.785.
kiln.h2_burnt_in_kiln_frac.source_file: Energy survey of the coal based sponge iron industry_Nishant R Dey et al
kiln.h2_burnt_in_kiln_frac.notes: Corroborated by Dey's Table 4 waste gas analysis, which finds only 0.17 vol% H2 and 0.59 vol% CH4 -- almost all coal hydrogen is oxidised by the sampling point. An earlier reading of this model derived 0.24 from the O2 demand of reaction [8] alone, which counts only injection-coal V.M. hydrogen and so understates kiln hydrogen combustion roughly threefold.

kiln.co_in_waste_gas_frac.source: Dey et al. (2015) Table 4 waste gas analysis: CO 1.32 vol%, CO2 34.91 vol%; CO/(CO+CO2) = 3.64 mol%.
kiln.co_in_waste_gas_frac.source_file: Energy survey of the coal based sponge iron industry_Nishant R Dey et al
kiln.co_in_waste_gas_frac.notes: Measured CO slip is small because Dey's sample point is downstream of post-combustion. Raise towards 0.15 to model a kiln-exit sample point.

kiln.radiation_loss_frac.source: Dey et al. (2015) Table 11 item [10]: radiation loss 8.00 Gcal/h against coal NHV input of 118.4 Gcal/h (13,990 kg/h x 22,530.2 kJ/kg + 7,730 kg/h x 23,362.02 kJ/kg) = 6.76%. Dey takes total wall loss as twice the kiln shell loss to cover the hoods, ABC and cooler inlet.
kiln.radiation_loss_frac.source_file: Energy survey of the coal based sponge iron industry_Nishant R Dey et al
kiln.radiation_loss_frac.notes: Expressed against coal NHV, not against 'reaction heat', so the term is unambiguous. As a share of Dey's reaction heat the same 8.00 Gcal/h is 12.3%.

kiln.waste_gas_cp_kj_kgk.source: Mean Cp of kiln waste gas over 25-900 degC.

power.aux_kwh_per_t_dri.source: CEEW: 'consumption is in the range of 55 kWh/t-DRI to 65 kWh/t-DRI'; survey also found some plants at 80-100 kWh/t-DRI
power.aux_kwh_per_t_dri.source_file: Decarbonising Coal-based DRI Production_Kartheek Nitturu et al
power.aux_kwh_per_t_dri.notes: Replaces the previous hardcoded 24 MWh/d, which was capacity-independent and equivalent to 267 kWh/t at 90 TPD - roughly 4x the surveyed value.

power.grid_ef_t_per_mwh.source: Indian grid emission factor. CEA CO2 Baseline Database is the standard citation - NOT present in this repository.

whr.boiler_efficiency.source: Engineering default for a waste heat recovery boiler.

whr.cycle_efficiency.source: Rankine cycle gross efficiency at sponge-iron WHRB steam conditions.

whr.abc_combustion_frac.source: Fraction of unburnt VM carbon and CO post-combusted in the after-burner chamber ahead of the WHRB.

whr.opex_frac_of_capex.source: Annual O&M as a fraction of CAPEX.

biomass.nhv_kj_kg.source: Agricultural residue / raw biomass net heating value (~3500 kcal/kg).

biomass.ash_frac.source: Rice husk is at the high end of this range.

biomass.char_reactivity.source: Vigneswaran et al. and Bhardwaj et al. both note biochar gasifies to CO more readily than coal char; this factor scales biomass carbon's availability as a reductant.
biomass.char_reactivity.source_file: Pathways for decarbonizing the sponge iron industries_Vigneswaran V S et al

biomass.price_inr_per_t.source: Engineering default. Fan and Friedmann quote $295-525/t for biomass, which is far above Indian agri-residue prices - do not use that range for India without justification.

biomass.biogenic_co2_zero_rated.source: IPCC convention: biogenic CO2 is reported separately from fossil CO2 and scored as zero in the fossil total. This is an ACCOUNTING CHOICE - set to 0 to see gross stack CO2.

biomass.max_substitution_frac.source: Upper bound imposed by kiln flame stability and biomass bulk density.

hydrogen.nhv_kj_kg.source: Lower heating value of H2 = 119.96 MJ/kg (28,660 kcal/kg).

hydrogen.price_inr_per_kg.source: Hall et al. (TERI): 'India, of around $3.5/kg, DRI from a hydrogen rotary kiln would be close to competitive'. Converted at INR 87/USD.
hydrogen.price_inr_per_kg.source_file: Hydrogen Rotary Kilns for Ironmaking in India_Will Hall et al

hydrogen.ef_t_per_t.source: Green (electrolytic, RE-powered) hydrogen assumed. Grey SMR hydrogen would be ~9-10 t CO2/t H2 - change this to test a grey-H2 sensitivity.

hydrogen.max_substitution_frac.source: Retrofit limit for an existing kiln. Full H2-DR needs 53.5-59.6 kg H2/t DRI (Kamal et al.), which is a greenfield shaft-furnace case, not a kiln retrofit.

econ.ore_price_inr_per_t.source: Engineering default; NMDC lump ore price is the standard reference.

econ.coal_price_inr_per_t.source: Engineering default for imported non-coking coal landed cost.

econ.power_tariff_inr_per_kwh.source: Industrial HT tariff. State-specific; cite the relevant SERC tariff order.

econ.export_tariff_inr_per_kwh.source: Surplus WHR power exported to the grid / sold via open access. Lower than the import tariff, which is why self-consumption is credited first.

econ.char_credit_inr_per_t.source: Dolochar sold to AFBC captive power plants and brick makers.

econ.fixed_opex_inr_per_day.source: Engineering default: labour, maintenance, refractory, overheads for a 100 TPD kiln.
econ.fixed_opex_inr_per_day.notes: Should scale with capacity; currently capacity-independent.

econ.discount_rate.source: Weighted average cost of capital for an Indian secondary steel producer.
